title: Purity and Worship
question: Why does prayer begin with water?
intro: Worship in Islam has a rhythm. The Quran sets the frame: wash before prayer, pray at set times, fast in Ramadan, give zakah (the yearly alms) to named groups, and travel to the House in Makkah for Hajj if able. The Prophet ﷺ showed the details, and Muslims learn them from his Sunnah, his example.

Running through every command is the same note of ease. The sick and the traveller have concessions, clean earth can stand in for water, and prayer can be shortened on a journey. "Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you" (5:6). Today you will see the verses behind daily worship, and how alcohol was forbidden in stages.

passages.from: O you who have believed, when you rise
passages.context: Madinan. It goes on to ghusl (a full wash) and tayammum with clean earth.
passages.point: Wudu in four acts: wash the face, the arms to the elbows, wipe the head, and the feet.
passages.label: differ
passages.note: Most read "your feet" with the washed parts, so the feet are washed. Shi'i scholars, following another recitation, read it with the head, so the feet are wiped.

passages.context: Makkan, from al-Isra. 11:114 and 4:103 also speak of prayer at set times.
passages.point: From the sun's decline to the dark of night, and at dawn. Scholars read this as covering Dhuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib, 'Isha and Fajr.
passages.label: explained

passages.context: Madinan, from al-Baqarah. The next verses excuse the sick and travellers, who make up the days (2:184-185).
passages.point: Fasting is not new: it was prescribed for those before. Its aim is taqwa, being mindful of Allah.
passages.label: stated

passages.context: Madinan, from at-Tawbah. The Quran pairs zakah with prayer many times (e.g. 2:43).
passages.point: Zakah goes to eight named groups: the poor, the needy, its collectors, hearts to be won, captives, debtors, Allah's cause, and stranded travellers.
passages.label: stated

visual.title: The prayer times and the sun
visual.caption: The Quran points to prayer at set times (4:103), naming dawn, the sun's decline and the night. The five times and their exact limits are detailed in the Sunnah.
visual.label: explained

items.label: Dhuhr
items.text: Just after the sun passes its height

items.label: 'Asr
items.text: Afternoon; many link "the middle prayer" to it

word.nuance: From ʿ-b-d, to serve; an ʿabd is a servant. ʿIbādah covers the set rituals, but also any good act done for Allah: honest work, kindness, care for family. "I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me" (51:56).

mixup.myth: Alcohol was forbidden in a single verse from the first day of Islam.
mixup.truth: Scholars commonly read the verses as stages: 2:219 says its sin is greater than its benefit; 4:43 forbids coming to prayer intoxicated; 5:90-91 commands avoiding it altogether. The early community already drank, and the change came over years in Madinah. Reports in al-Bukhari say that when the final verse came, people poured out their wine.

remember: Purity comes first: wudu, ghusl after janabah, and tayammum with clean earth when water is lacking (5:6).
Prayer has set times; the Quran points to them and the Sunnah details all five (4:103, 17:78).
Fasting, zakah to eight groups, and Hajj for those able, each with ease built in (2:183-185, 9:60, 3:97).

quiz.q: What does 5:6 allow for purification when there is no water?
quiz.why: 5:6: "...and do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it." This is tayammum; 4:43 says the same.

quiz.q: Who does 3:97 say owes Allah the pilgrimage to the House?
options: Whoever is able to find a way
quiz.why: 3:97: "And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House - for whoever is able to find thereto a way."

quiz.q: What does 22:37 say reaches Allah from an animal sacrifice?
options: The piety of the one who offers it
quiz.why: 22:37: "Their meat will not reach Allah, nor will their blood, but what reaches Him is piety from you."

reflect: Which act of worship feels most natural to you right now, and which would you most like to understand better?
